descripcion_es: -er/-est, more/most, as… as and irregular forms.
resumen: The comparative compares two things (bigger than, more expensive than) and the superlative picks out one within a group (the biggest, the most expensive). The form depends on the length of the adjective.

filas: Two or more syllables: modern, expensive
the most modern / the most expensive

items: Equality: as + adjective + as. This room is as big as yours.
Negative inequality: not as + adjective + as. The film wasn't as good as the book.
Inferiority: less + adjective + than (more common with long adjectives). It's less expensive than I thought.
After the superlative, in is used with places or groups (the tallest in the class) and of with periods or quantities (the best day of my life).

explicacion.texto: Than is the equivalent of Spanish “que” in comparisons; that is never used. More and -er are not combined either: more cheaper is incorrect.

ejemplos.frase: My new flat is bigger than the old one.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mi piso nuevo es más grande que el antiguo.

ejemplos.frase: This is the most interesting book I've read this year.
ejemplos.traduccion: Es el libro más interesante que he leído este año.

ejemplos.frase: Valencia isn't as cold as Burgos.
ejemplos.traduccion: Valencia no es tan fría como Burgos.

ejemplos.frase: She's the best player in the team.
ejemplos.traduccion: Es la mejor jugadora del equipo.

ejemplos.frase: Trains are usually more comfortable than buses.
ejemplos.traduccion: Los trenes suelen ser más cómodos que los autobuses.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She is more tall than me.
He is the oldest of the family.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: He is the oldest in the family.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With groups or places we use in, not of (Spanish “de”).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: My car is faster that yours.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: My car is faster than yours.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the comparative of the adjective.
ejercicios.frase: A bicycle is ___ (cheap) than a motorbike.
respuestas: cheaper
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the first table for one-syllable adjectives: they add -er in the comparative. The clue is than after the gap, which requires a comparative, and the fact that cheap has one syllable. That is why cheap becomes cheaper, without more.
ejercicios.traduccion: Una bicicleta es más barata que una moto.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Calque of Spanish “más barato”: one-syllable adjectives do not use more, but -er.
The card explicitly forbids it: more and -er are not combined.
It is the superlative; with than the comparative cheaper is needed.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the comparative of the adjective.
ejercicios.frase: This exercise is ___ (difficult) than the last one.
respuestas: more difficult
ejercicios.explicacion: The first table shows that adjectives of two or more syllables form the comparative with more + adjective. Difficult has three syllables (dif-fi-cult) and is followed by than, so the form is more difficult. -er is never added to it.
ejercicios.traduccion: Este ejercicio es más difícil que el anterior.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Long adjectives do not take -er; we use more difficult.
More and -er are not combined; more difficult is enough.
Most is for the superlative; with than we use more.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the superlative of the adjective.
ejercicios.frase: August is the ___ (hot) month of the year in Seville.
respuestas: hottest
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the rule in the first table for one-syllable adjectives ending in consonant-vowel-consonant: they double the final consonant (big, biggest). Hot follows that pattern, so the superlative is hottest. The superlative clue is the before and of the year after: one month is picked out within a period, and that is why of is used.
ejercicios.traduccion: Agosto es el mes más caluroso del año en Sevilla.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The t has not been doubled: hot ends in consonant-vowel-consonant and becomes hottest.
Hot has one syllable and forms the superlative with -est, not with most.
It is the comparative; with the and of the year the superlative is needed.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the comparative of the adjective.
ejercicios.frase: My cold is ___ (bad) today than yesterday.
respuestas: worse
ejercicios.explicacion: Bad is one of the irregular adjectives in the second table: bad, worse, the worst. The clue is than, which requires a comparative, and the contrast today / yesterday. That is why the form is worse, without -er or more.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi resfriado está peor hoy que ayer.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Bad is irregular; its comparative is worse.
Calque of Spanish “más malo”: the comparative of bad is worse.
Worst is the superlative (the worst); with than we use worse.

glosario.definicion_l: having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness or having been made cold by e.g. ice or refrigeration · extended meanings; especially of psychological coldness; without human warmth or emotion

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the superlative of the adjective.
ejercicios.frase: That was the ___ (happy) day of my life.
respuestas: happiest
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table for two-syllable adjectives ending in -y: the y changes to i and -est is added (easy, the easiest). Happy is of that type, so the superlative is happiest. The clue is the before and of my life after, which, according to the card, takes of because it is a period.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Two syllables ending in -y: happy → happiest.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ese fue el día más feliz de mi vida.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y use -est: happiest.
The y changes to i before -est: happiest.
It is the comparative; with the and of my life the superlative is needed.

respuestas: bigger
ejercicios.explicacion: Big has one syllable and ends in consonant-vowel-consonant, so according to the table it doubles the g and adds -er: bigger. The clue is than, which requires a comparative. It is exactly the example on the card.
ejercicios.traduccion: Madrid es más grande que Toledo.

por_opcion.more big: Incorrect: calque of Spanish “más grande”; a one-syllable adjective does not use more.
por_opcion.bigger: Correct: comparative of big, doubling the g, and it goes with than.
por_opcion.biggest: Incorrect: it is the superlative, which would go with the and not with than.

respuestas: best
ejercicios.explicacion: Good is irregular according to the second table: good, better, the best. The clue is the before the gap and in town after it, which indicate a superlative within a place. That is why the form is best: the best restaurant in town.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Irregular superlative of good: the best.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es el mejor restaurante de la ciudad.

por_opcion.better: Incorrect: it is the comparative (better than), which does not go with the or with in town.
por_opcion.goodest: Incorrect: it does not exist; good is irregular.
por_opcion.best: Correct: irregular superlative of good, the best.

ejercicios.frase: Tom is as tall ___ his father.
respuestas: as
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the comparative of equality from the card's list: as + adjective + as. The clue is the first as before tall, which requires another as after it. Spanish “tan… como” is always translated as as… as.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tom es tan alto como su padre.

por_opcion.than: Incorrect: than goes after a comparative (taller than), not after as.
por_opcion.as: Correct: it completes the structure of equality as tall as.
por_opcion.that: Incorrect: that is never used in comparisons, either of equality or of superiority.

ejercicios.frase: She is the youngest ___ her class.
respuestas: in
ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that after the superlative, in is used with places or groups and of with periods or quantities. Her class is a group, so it takes in. Spanish “de su clase” pushes towards of, which is the typical error noted on the card.
ejercicios.traduccion: Es la más joven de su clase.

por_opcion.of: Incorrect here: calque of Spanish “de”; with a group or a place we use in. Of would go with periods or quantities (of the year, of the three).
por_opcion.in: Correct: superlative followed by a group, the youngest in her class.
por_opcion.than: Incorrect: than goes with comparatives, not with superlatives.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence with not as ... as, without changing the meaning.
ejercicios.frase: My phone is older than yours.
respuestas: My phone isn't as new as yours.
My phone is not as new as yours.
Your phone isn't as old as mine.
Your phone is not as old as mine.
Yours isn't as old as mine.
Yours is not as old as mine.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the negative inequality on the card: not as + adjective + as. If my phone is older, you can say that it is not as new as yours or, changing the subject, that yours is not as old as mine. That is why both perspectives are accepted, with or without a contraction, and with yours instead of your phone. You have to change the adjective or the order of the terms so that the meaning is not reversed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Not as ... as expresses that something does not reach the same degree.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi teléfono no es tan nuevo como el tuyo (o: tu teléfono no es tan viejo como el mío).

errores_previstos.respuesta: My phone isn't as old as yours.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It reverses the meaning: it would say that my phone is newer. You have to change old to new or swap the terms.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My phone isn't as new than yours.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The structure of equality is as … as; than only goes with comparatives.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My phone isn't so new like yours.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Like does not work in this structure; it is as … as.

ejercicios.frase: This sofa is more comfortabler than the other one.
respuestas: This sofa is more comfortable than the other one.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card insists that more and -er are not combined. Comfortable is long (three or four syllables), so its comparative is more comfortable. The sentence has both markers at once, more and -er, and the -er must be removed.
ejercicios.traduccion: Este sofá es más cómodo que el otro.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This sofa is more comfortabler than the other one.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: more and -er are not combined.

errores_previstos.respuesta: This sofa is comfortabler than the other one.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Comfortable is a long adjective and does not take -er; we use more.

ejercicios.frase: Her English is better that mine.
respuestas: Her English is better than mine.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card says so in its final text: Spanish “que” in comparisons is than, never that. The clue is the comparative better, which is always followed by than. Better is correct (irregular comparative of good); only that needs to be changed.
ejercicios.traduccion: Su inglés es mejor que el mío.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Her English is better that mine.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: after a comparative comes than.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Her English is more good than mine.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Than has been fixed but the comparative has been spoilt: good is irregular, better.

ejercicios.frase: It was the most bad film I've ever seen.
respuestas: It was the worst film I've ever seen.
It was the worst film I have ever seen.
ejercicios.explicacion: Bad is irregular according to the second table and its superlative is the worst, not the most bad. The clue is the superlative with the and the tag I've ever seen, typical of superlatives. It is enough to change most bad to worst; the contraction I've can be written in full.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Irregular superlative of bad: the worst.
ejercicios.traduccion: Fue la peor película que he visto nunca.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It was the most bad film I've ever seen.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: bad is irregular and its superlative is the worst.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It was the baddest film I've ever seen.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Baddest does not exist in standard English; the superlative is worst.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It was the worse film I've ever seen.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Worse is the comparative (worse than); with the and ever seen we use the superlative worst.

respuestas: London is more expensive than Paris
Paris is more expensive than London
ejercicios.explicacion: The structure is subject + is + more + adjective + than + second term. Expensive is long, so it goes with more. The words allow either of the two cities to be the subject, and both sentences are grammatically correct, which is why both are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Subject + is + more + adjective + than + second term.
ejercicios.traduccion: Londres es más cara que París (o: París es más cara que Londres).

errores_previstos.respuesta: London is expensive more than Paris
errores_previstos.explicacion: More goes before the adjective: more expensive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: London more expensive is than Paris
errores_previstos.explicacion: The verb is goes right after the subject.

respuestas: Everest is the highest mountain in the world
The highest mountain in the world is Everest
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the structure the + superlative + noun + in + place. Highest is the superlative of high (one syllable, -est), and the world is a place, so it takes in, not of. The sentence can begin with Everest or with The highest mountain; both sentences are correct.
ejercicios.traduccion: El Everest es la montaña más alta del mundo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Everest is the mountain highest in the world
errores_previstos.explicacion: The superlative adjective goes before the noun: the highest mountain.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Everest is the highest mountain the in world
errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition goes before the article: in the world.

descripcion_larga_es: The comparative compares two things (cheaper than, more expensive than) and the superlative picks out one within a group (the cheapest, the most expensive). In English the form depends on the length of the adjective: short ones add -er and -est and long ones use more and most. Spanish speakers find it difficult because in Spanish everything is done with “más”, which is why they say more cheap, more cheaper or that instead of than.

contexto.que_es: They are the adjective forms used to compare. The comparative of superiority uses -er or more + than; the comparative of equality, as + adjective + as; the comparative of inferiority, less + adjective + than or not as … as. The superlative uses the + -est or the most, followed by in or of depending on the group.
contexto.por_que_importa: Comparing is a basic communicative function: choosing products, describing cities, assessing options or presenting economic data (higher, lower, the largest). Errors such as more big, more cheaper or better that mine are very noticeable and are penalised in any exam from A2 upwards.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: Whenever two things are related to each other or one is picked out among several. The signals are than, as … as, the and words such as ever, in the world or of my life. Spanish speakers, who use “más” for everything, must first look at the number of syllables in the adjective and remember the irregular forms good, bad and far.
